title: Grass on Denim
timeEstimate: 15–40 minutes; protein + chlorophyll combo, indigo dye-loss risk
stainChemistry: Grass is two stains in one: green chlorophyll pigment from the leaf plus plant protein the chlorophyll is bound to. The pigment is alcohol-soluble (rubbing alcohol pulls it out). The protein responds to cool water + Dawn. Hot water at any step sets the protein side and locks the green; once green sets, indigo denim is hard to recover without losing color too. Denim has its own complications: indigo sits on the surface of the fiber, and oxidizers such as peroxide, oxygen bleach, or chlorine bleach can pull color along with the stain. Aggressive scrubbing on raw or dark denim leaves a halo ring around the treated spot. The recurring trap is reaching for hot water to 'lift' fresh grass — that's exactly what locks it.
whyThisWorks: Cool water plus Dawn handles the protein component without setting it. Isopropyl alcohol on a white cloth can pull the green chlorophyll out, but dark, indigo, raw, selvage, black-overdyed, and high-value denim need a hidden test first and immediate stop if blue or black dye transfers. Air-dry is non-negotiable until the stain is gone — once the dryer hits residual chlorophyll, it sets permanently and adds polymer locking from the protein side.
defaultAssumption: Kid soccer / yard work / lawn-tackle on dark or medium-wash denim. Fresh = high-confidence DIY. Hot-dried or sat-for-weeks = much harder; pro for dark indigo denim. Raw / selvage denim = pro from minute one (any moisture causes uneven fading).

spottingProtocol.instruction: Damp white cloth with COOL water. Press, lift, rotate. Cool only — heat sets the protein side. Never pour water directly on denim — causes water rings.
Drop of Dawn on damp cloth. Soft toothbrush. Always blot, never rub — denim ring-stains under aggressive scrubbing. Cool damp-cloth rinse.

Inside seam test: dampen a white cloth or Q-tip with 91% IPA, dab an inside seam for 30 seconds, then blot with a clean white cloth. If blue or black dye transfers, skip alcohol and stop home treatment. If the test stays clean, continue cautiously and stop immediately if color transfers, a pale halo appears, or texture changes.

spottingProtocol.equipment: 91% IPA on white cotton cloth, ventilation
spottingProtocol.instruction: Apply 91% IPA to a clean white cloth — never pour on denim. Tamp the green spot from the top in short outside-in passes, flipping the cloth as it picks up green. Stop immediately if denim color transfers, a pale halo appears, or texture changes. Open windows; flammable, no flame.

spottingProtocol.equipment: Normal detergent, COOL water, washing machine
spottingProtocol.instruction: After the Dawn step and any alcohol step that passed hidden testing, wash the whole garment with normal detergent on a cool cycle, following the care label. Do not use hot water, chlorine bleach, or oxygen bleach on dark indigo, raw, selvage, black-overdyed, non-colorfast, embellished, or high-value denim.
AIR-DRY. Inspect in daylight. Faint green = repeat alcohol pass before the dryer touches it. Hot dryer on residual chlorophyll = permanent on denim plus indigo lock together.

steps: 3. Hidden-seam IPA test on indigo / dark denim.
4. 91% IPA cloth tamp for chlorophyll, outside-in, 2–3 passes.
5. Cool machine wash with normal detergent, following the care label.
6. Air-dry plus daylight inspect — never heat until clear.

homeSolutions.agent: Two Stains in One — Pigment Plus Protein
homeSolutions.instruction: Grass is the green pigment plus plant protein. Each part needs different treatment: cool Dawn for the protein side, rubbing alcohol for the green. Doing only one half is why grass stains come back after the first wash. Two hard rules on denim: NO hot water (sets the protein, locks the green) and NO chlorine bleach (strips indigo unevenly, leaves a halo).

Damp a white cloth with COOL water. Press the spot, lift, rotate to a clean section, press again. Cool only. Never pour water directly on denim — it causes water rings that are their own stain. Always blot, never rub — rubbing causes a halo on dark denim.

homeSolutions.agent: Dawn First — Cut the Protein Side
homeSolutions.instruction: Drop of Dawn on a damp cloth. Work it into the spot with a soft toothbrush for 5 minutes. Damp-cloth rinse. This handles the protein part of the stain. The chlorophyll is still in there — the alcohol step pulls it out next.

homeSolutions.agent: Hidden-Seam Test on Dark or Raw Denim
homeSolutions.instruction: Before any alcohol on dark, indigo, raw, selvage, black-overdyed, or high-value denim: dampen a white cloth or Q-tip with 91% isopropyl alcohol, dab an inside seam for 30 seconds, then blot with a clean white cloth. If any blue or black dye transfers, skip alcohol and stop home treatment. If the test stays clean, continue cautiously and stop immediately if denim color transfers, a pale halo appears, or texture changes.

homeSolutions.agent: Isopropyl Alcohol on a Cloth — Pulls Out the Green
homeSolutions.instruction: Apply 91% isopropyl alcohol to a clean white cloth — never pour on the denim. Tamp the green spot in short outside-in passes, flip the cloth as it picks up green, repeat. Stop immediately if denim color transfers, a pale halo appears, or texture changes. Open windows — alcohol is flammable, no flame.

After the Dawn step and any alcohol step that passed hidden testing, wash the whole garment with normal detergent on a cool cycle, following the care label. Do not use hot water, chlorine bleach, or oxygen bleach on dark indigo, raw, selvage, black-overdyed, non-colorfast, embellished, or high-value denim. Air-dry and inspect in daylight before any dryer heat.

homeSolutions.agent: Air-Dry and Inspect Before Any Dryer Heat
homeSolutions.instruction: Hang to AIR-DRY. Inspect in daylight before the dryer goes anywhere near it. Faint green left? Repeat the alcohol pass. Only put it in the dryer once the stain is invisible in natural light. Hot dryer on residual chlorophyll = permanent on denim.

steps: 1. NO hot water. NO chlorine bleach.
2. Cool damp-cloth blot — never pour, never rub.
4. Hidden-seam IPA test on dark / raw denim before alcohol.
5. 91% IPA on cloth, tamp green spot outside-in, 2–3 passes.
6. Cool machine wash with normal detergent, following the care label.
7. AIR-DRY plus daylight inspect — no dryer until fully clear.

escalation.when: Hot water or hot dryer already used (often permanent). Hidden-seam IPA test shows indigo loss. Raw / selvage / black-overdyed denim. 2 home rounds plateau. Halo ring already forming around the spot.

No hot, no chlorine, no oxygen bleach on dark/raw/non-colorfast denim. [Residual green / halo ring / indigo loss / hot-dried suspected]."

deepSolveHooks.modifierNotes: Indigo dye loss is the recurring trap on denim. Hidden-seam IPA test is the safety check. Raw / selvage denim is pro from minute one because any moisture causes uneven fading. Black overdyed denim is similarly fragile. Mud + grass = brush mud off dry first, then run grass protocol. Hot-dried grass on denim is often permanent; managing expectations is part of the protocol.
